about.description: Terminal dashboard for GitHub — followers, stars, PRs and issues at a glance, auto-refreshed
about.head: 85711f9

name: v0.36.0
body:
**Someone to wait with, a refresh that follows yours, and a scan that stops mixing branches.** octoscope has a face now — an octopus with a periscope, drawn in the terminal's own block characters — and two quieter changes underneath it: pressing `r` finally moves the automatic refresh, and the supply-chain scan no longer scores a capability that exists on no single branch.

## An octopus heads every screen before the dashboard

Every screen before the dashboard — loading, the sponsor splash, help, a first-fetch error — now opens with a small octopus and its periscope. While your data loads it looks around, turns its periscope with its eyes, blinks and curls its tentacles, and the splash now says it is loading too. ([#200](https://github.com/gfazioli/octoscope/pull/200))

Once the dashboard is up, a smaller one stays beside the banner when the window is wide enough, facing ahead, and looks around again whenever a refresh runs — yours or the automatic one. ([#201](https://github.com/gfazioli/octoscope/pull/201))

Both take your theme's colours, monochromatic themes and `NO_COLOR` draw them as a one-colour silhouette, and they add no delay: they move with the spinner and stop with it.

They are drawn with Unicode's quadrant block characters (U+2596–U+259F), four pixels to a cell, which octoscope uses for the first time in this release. A terminal font without those glyphs will show replacement characters where the octopus should be; nothing else in the interface uses them.

## Your refresh moves the automatic one

Only the answer to a fetch the timer itself had started used to reschedule the next automatic refresh, so pressing `r`, the startup fetch and a settings refetch never moved the timer already pending. After an `r` that came back rate-limited, the automatic refresh fired on the old cadence anyway and spent one more request against the limit. Closes [#202](https://github.com/gfazioli/octoscope/issues/202). ([#204](https://github.com/gfazioli/octoscope/pull/204))

Now the answer to every fetch arms the next automatic refresh from what that answer said — the interval, or the back-off after a primary rate limit — and supersedes the tick pending before, so exactly one stays live. An interval change keeps a back-off that is still in force. Measured against GitHub with a 30-second interval, pressing `r` five seconds after the startup answer: before, the next automatic fetch went out 7 seconds after `r`'s answer, on the old cadence; now it goes out 30 seconds after it.

The automatic refresh also no longer starts a second fetch while yours is still running, which stopped the spinner early and could let an older answer replace a newer one. ([#201](https://github.com/gfazioli/octoscope/pull/201))

One limit is older than this release, and now documented rather than fixed: the reset time arrives with a successful refresh, so a session whose very first fetch already hits the primary limit has none to wait for, and retries at the interval.

## The scan stops mixing branches

The capability axis parses workflows from every branch it walks, and scored them as if every copy were reachable. Two corrections:

- **A trigger scores only where its branch can start it.** GitHub starts outsider events only from the default branch — `pull_request_target` included, on github.com, checked against the event reference's own `GITHUB_REF` column — so a privileged workflow sitting on a topic branch no longer counts. It is still listed, with the branch it would have to reach, and an unknown default branch filters nothing, so the axis cannot go silent by accident. Closes [#188](https://github.com/gfazioli/octoscope/issues/188). ([#196](https://github.com/gfazioli/octoscope/pull/196))
- **A trigger and a secret must share a branch.** The per-branch results were merged by path, so a trigger from one branch's copy of a workflow was scored with a secret or a write grant from another branch's copy — two harmless files could add up to a score of 3 for a capability that existed on neither. Each branch's copy is judged on its own now. Closes [#197](https://github.com/gfazioli/octoscope/issues/197). ([#198](https://github.com/gfazioli/octoscope/pull/198))

This moves scores **down** for repositories with long-lived branches. That is the correction, not a lost signal.

## The site moves

The landing's sections now arrive on the same springs as the promo films, sampled into CSS `linear()` curves by a Go test rather than typed by hand, and nothing is hidden before the script has run and measured it off screen: a script that fails costs the motion, never the content. The launch octopus — the TUI's own drawing, held to `mascot.go` by a test — walks in beside the screenshot carousel and says what each shot shows. It stays away at 64em or below, where its bubble would run into the next section; under Reduce Motion it arrives standing; and keyboard focus reveals whatever it lands on. ([#203](https://github.com/gfazioli/octoscope/pull/203))

## Notable polish

- Every landing still was regenerated with the mini octopus in the banner, and "At a glance" gained a card for it.
- The "At a glance" cards are only as tall as their content.
- Reduce Motion now also stops smooth anchor scrolling and the transitions of the carousel dots and the newsletter prompt.

## Tests

- The refresh timer's tests read what was armed — its delay and its generation — through the `tickCmd` seam instead of inferring it from a non-nil batch, and count dispatched fetches through `fetchCmd`; the rate-limit sequence starts from the `r` key itself. Ten mutations each fail a test, among them the old self-re-arming tick, the race it prevented, an answer that arms nothing and arming without the generation bump.
- The landing is held by Go tests: the springs must be the generated ones; no rule may hide a reveal element unless it requires a scope the script armed, checked on what each rule declares at any depth of `@media` and `@supports`; every variant has a pose; the site's octopus must be the TUI's. Each was validated by breaking what it protects, and they pass on the Windows runner's CRLF checkout, which failed their first run.
- The scan's new behaviour tests each assert a control on the default branch first: "it does not score" passes just as well when the axis has stopped working.
- The mascot is tested to take its colours from the active theme.

## Upgrade

```
brew upgrade gfazioli/tap/octoscope
```
